metaData.title: The Implementation of AI Shopping Assistant on vivo's Official Website
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the implementation of an AI shopping assistant on vivo's official website, utilizing intent recognition models, Agent workflows, RAG knowledge bases, and structured output to recommend phones and answer parameter-related questions.
metaData.summary: This article systematically describes the entire process from technology selection to implementation of the AI shopping assistant feature in vivo's official website app. First, by comparing three approaches—fine-tuning large models, building dedicated models, and using Agent workflows—the Agent workflow was chosen based on cost-effectiveness, technical risk, and business suitability. The overall architecture adopts a four-layer design: Application Layer, Strategy Layer, Jiuwen Layer (Agent platform), and Xuanji Layer (large model computation). Core solutions include: using a FastText small model for intent recognition (inference time ~10ms), designing two agents for phone parameter interpretation and product recommendation, enhancing answer accuracy through Prompt engineering and RAG knowledge bases, and achieving structured display of product cards, large model streaming output, and related posts. After launch, the first-character response time was controlled within 2.5 seconds, positively contributing to business GMV and resolution rate.

mainPoints.point: Choosing the Agent workflow approach over fine-tuning large models or building dedicated models.
mainPoints.explanation: Based on a comprehensive evaluation of cost-effectiveness, technical risk control, business suitability, and maintenance costs, the Agent workflow approach demonstrated the best performance in development cost, generalization capability, and iteration efficiency.

mainPoints.point: Using a FastText small model for intent recognition with an inference time of approximately 10ms.
mainPoints.explanation: By training a FastText text classification model with synthetic data to replace large language models for front-end intent recognition, response latency is significantly reduced while maintaining accuracy, and it can run efficiently on CPUs.

mainPoints.point: Adopting a combined strategy of Prompt engineering + RAG knowledge base + information interface engineering.
mainPoints.explanation: Through carefully designed Prompts to constrain model behavior boundaries, utilizing RAG to retrieve relevant fragments from product recommendation and review knowledge bases, and combining engineering capabilities such as product APIs and intelligent customer service, a high-quality information set is constructed and fed into the large model.

mainPoints.point: Achieving structured display of product cards, large model outputs, and related posts.
mainPoints.explanation: By engineering means to combine large model outputs with backend interface data, dynamically inserting product cards and community post information into the streaming output, enhancing user experience and information richness.

keyQuotes: Broadly speaking, an AI shopping assistant is a comprehensive agent that users can engage in multi-turn conversations with; narrowly speaking, it is a system that works through information processing engineering and large language models to understand user intent and respond to user questions under constrained conditions.

When building an AI shopping assistant, it is essential to clearly define the capability boundaries of the solution, i.e., to have a clear understanding of the AI shopping assistant's role in the vivo website scenario. Therefore, from the outset, the goal was not to be 'big and comprehensive,' but 'small and precise.'

Through a layered design, each layer can more clearly understand its own responsibilities. As long as the interface between layers is properly connected, there is no need to worry about the implementation details of other layers.

All recommended phone product information is supplemented into the phone recommendation list according to certain rules, then combined with the Prompt and sent to the large model together. This allows the large model to understand the user's query, find the most suitable phone from the recommendation list, and provide a recommendation reason.

relatedArticles.title: VAPD AgentKit: A Composable Frontend General-Purpose Library for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the VAPD AgentKit, a composable Agent frontend general-purpose library developed by the vivo team, based on a unified message model, Runtime Adapter, and frontend orchestration, designed to provide a unified conversational AI capability foundation for businesses like notes, knowledge bases, and project management.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Agent Architecture Design: Insights from OpenClaw
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth breakdown of the architectural design of mainstream Agents like OpenClaw and Claude Code, analyzing the pros and cons of key decisions across four dimensions: context management, tool loading, tool discovery, and main loop design.

relatedArticles.title: In-Depth Analysis of vivo's Activity System Globalization Practices
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the complete technical practices and architectural evolution of vivo's activity system during globalization, from internationalization (multi-language, multi-timezone, multi-tenancy, data storage) to global co-line (unified architecture, unified domain name, handling external dependency differences).

relatedArticles.title: From 7.9% to 54% Adoption: The Three-Stage Evolution of Kuaishou's Intelligent Code Review
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the three-generation architectural evolution of Kuaishou's intelligent code review system—from pure LLM heuristics to knowledge engine-driven, and finally to Agentic autonomous decision-making—increasing the CR adoption rate from 7.9% to 54%.

relatedArticles.title: E45 Meng Yan in Conversation with Li Jigang: How Humans Find Their Place
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This episode explores the inevitable transition from mental labor to 'heart power' in the AI era, and the deep philosophy of responding to technological change by reconstructing investment, education, and mental models.

relatedArticles.title: The Practice of Implementing the Next-Generation Image Format AVIF in the vivo Community
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the practical experience of the vivo community in introducing the AVIF image format through a CDN edge caching and server-side asynchronous transcoding solution, achieving an additional 20%+ reduction in image size compared to WebP, which had already been fully adopted.

relatedArticles.title: A Possible Path for OpenClaw to Land in Real-World Production Applications
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the successful experience of Coding Agents, this article proposes that for business Agents (like OpenClaw) to land in production, the key is to reconstruct the open, decentralized, and hard-to-rollback business environment into a visualized, relatively closed, verifiable, and recoverable engineering operation space, and provides a specific path including visualization, closure, verification, and rollback layers.

relatedArticles.title: Dissecting OpenClaw: Understanding the Inner Workings of AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: By analyzing the open-source project OpenClaw, this article reveals how AI Agents utilize system prompts, tool calling, memory management, and heartbeat mechanisms to transform simple "text completion" models into intelligent systems capable of autonomous task execution.
